title: Sundial Health — privacy & edge deploy checklist (raw notes)
content:
Meeting: 2025-01-14 11:00 PT (technical pre-onramp)
Attendees: Asha (RWI), Ben (RWI), Marta (RWI solutions), Priya (Sundial eng lead), Jonah (Sundial infra), Legal: TBD

Quick summary:
- Sundial Health is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for PHI-containing Q&A and triage workflows. Their constraints are strict: HIPAA + state-level data residency for CA patient records, HSM-based key control, and 3-year audit retention.
- Primary ask: a deploy pattern that keeps inference inside their Azure tenancy with customer-managed keys, predictable 99th-pct latency <= 200ms for short prompts, and clear fallback behavior during node failures.

Notes from call (raw):
- Customer stack: Azure (eastus, westus2), AKS for app, want Redwood Private control plane in their VNet or peered with RWI mgmt? Prefer customer-only control plane (air-gapped-ish) but open to lightweight agent.
- Data flow they imagine: user -> app -> Redwood Private endpoint (in VNet) -> model inference -> app. No logs leave tenant unless explicitly exported to RWI support bundle.
- KMS: They use Azure Key Vault with HSM-protected keys. Need an integration plan: RWI Private must accept keys (wrap/unwrap) or use a bring-your-own-HSM connector.
- Audit: 3-year retention for request/response metadata (not full PHI) + request provenance. Need export hooks to their SIEM (Azure Sentinel).
- Embeddings: they want short-term embeddings for semantic search; retention policy: 30 days unless labelled persistent. Encryption-at-rest and in-transit mandatory.

Performance / capacity (customer estimates):
- Expected steady-state: 120 req/min during business hours, peaks 400 req/min for triage bot (avg 150 tokens/request).
- Latency target: median < 80ms, p95 < 200ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens).
- Model preference: prefer an open model family (for licensing); suggested families discussed: Llama2-13B-ish for triage, possibly quantized; fallback: smaller 7B variant for degraded capacity.
- Throughput idea: 2 dedicated GPUs (A10 / A100-p4) in each region + autoscale policy for peak. Need cost/latency tradeoff examples.

Security & compliance gotchas (explicit):
- PHI in prompts: they need a deterministic redaction/PII-filter before send (customer-side). RWI can optionally run a redaction filter but they want that to be opt-in.
- KV cache: must ensure cached KV items are encrypted with tenant keys and TTL is configurable. If we store prefix cache, must have ability to purge on demand for DSAR/retention.
- Support access: they disallow RWI staff SSH into nodes. Support bundle must be fully automated and provide only non-PHI traces unless they explicitly allow a deeper bundle.
- Canary rollouts: require traffic shadowing first, then 1% canary for 24h, then 10% for 6h before full. Need rollback within 5 minutes.

Open questions (we promised to clarify):
1) Control plane topology: do they want RWI-managed control plane in their VNet (private endpoint) or full customer-managed control plane?
2) HSM connector specifics: which Key Vault SKUs, any KMIP requirements, and who holds the wrap key?
3) Logs: exact retention policy for request metadata vs full payloads (they prefer no payload retention). Define fields we store in audit logs.
4) Network egress: confirm whether outbound to RWI (for model profiling/telemetry) is allowed over an endpoint or must be fully blocked.
5) Model licensing: confirm whether Llama2-family acceptable given their legal team; otherwise discuss RWI-curated permissive models.

Action items / next steps (owner + ETA):
- Asha: Draft proposal for control plane options (customer-managed vs RWI-lite) with pros/cons and ops tasks. ETA: 2025-01-21.
- Ben: Capacity cost sketch for two deployment shapes (dedicated GPUs per region vs central multi-region with cross-region routing) including estimated monthly spend and expected p95 latencies. ETA: 2025-01-24.
- Marta: KMS/HSM integration checklist + KMIP/Key Vault SKU compatibility notes. Include sample terraform snippet. ETA: 2025-01-22.
- Priya (Sundial): Confirm legal signoff risk tolerance for open model families and return list of acceptable model licenses. ETA: 2025-01-28.
- Jonah (Sundial): Provide network diagram and confirm whether peering or private endpoint preferred + egress rules. ETA: 2025-01-20.

Quick reference snippets to paste into OSS/PRs later:
- "Fallback policy: route to quantized-7b model in same region when model queue depth > 300ms or node OOM detected; degrade to non-PHI-only mode (response template) when policy trigger hits >2 events/min."
- "Cache purge API: POST /admin/cache/purge?tenant_id=XXX -- must accept purge token signed by tenant KMS."

Potential risks + mitigation ideas:
- Risk: Unexpected p95 spikes under batching if many concurrent short requests. Mitigation: dynamic batching override for tenants flagged as low-latency; set max_batch_size=4 and prefer immediate exec for <128-token requests.
- Risk: DSAR demands require full payload retention by regulators. Mitigation: offer export endpoints for raw payloads under customer control; require legal POA.

Loose notes / freeform (things to remember):
- They emphasized "no surprise traffic to outside US" — ensure regional routing maps to eastus/westus2 only.
- They would like a lightweight UI in Redwood Console showing KMS key status + last key rotation date.
- Suggest a pilot: start with non-PHI synthetic dataset for 2 weeks, then apply for PHI enablement after security review.

Links mentioned on call:
- Jira: INF-9812 (Sundial onramp epic)
- Confluence onboarding playbook (link above)
- Internal PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-proposals/pull/47

Notes to self (Asha):
- Bring up canary rollback automation: how do we detect a model-quality regression quickly? Connect Eval sets + prompt-SLO monitors.
- Draft sample SLA language for latency and key-holding responsibilities.
- Prep for legal: matrix of acceptable model licenses + example indemnities.

End of raw notes. Will refine into a tidy client-facing doc after action items resolve.
